section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the revelation of Chassidus, founded by the Baal Shem Tov and the Alter Rebbe on Chai Elul, to the principle that all matters must be drawn down into revealed understanding.
section.t: And one must connect this with the revelation of the Torah of Chassidus,
for Chai Elul is the birthday of the Baal Shem Tov, founder of the general Torah of Chassidus, and of the Alter Rebbe, founder of the Torah of Chabad Chassidus,
[such] that one of the main emphases in the Torah of Chassidus is that all matters should be drawn down below in revelation.
And as the Alter Rebbe wrote in Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmunah at its beginning: "It is written,
'Forever, O G-d, Your word stands firm in the heavens.'

And the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, explained that 'Your word'—that which You said, 'Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters,' etc.—these letters and words stand and endure forever within the firmament of the heavens, etc.,"
for even though this explanation is found in the Midrash Tehillim on the verse
(as brought in Likkutei Torah),
nevertheless, the Alter Rebbe writes "And the Baal Shem Tov, of blessed memory, explained,"
[and] one of the explanations of this
is that the Baal Shem Tov explained
(spread out)
and revealed this so that it would be known to all.
And the Alter Rebbe drew this down into intellect,
so that it would be for praise and for a name and for glory,
which refers to Chabad,
until this is grasped even in the intellect of the animal soul,
and even in the intellect of those who were
(before they learned this matter)
heretics,
"to set you high above all the nations."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that when Israel declares G-d's Oneness in Shema and Tefillin, they cause G-d to wear Tefillin, which are His glory, and that Israel's power to do so comes from G-d's declaration of them as His treasured people.
section.t: And this is [the meaning of] "You have declared G-d... you have made Him a single entity in the world, as it is said, 'Hear O Israel, G-d is our G-d, G-d is One,'"
for by Israel saying "G-d is One" in the Shema,
and especially in Tefillin,
by which they draw down "G-d is One" even into the physical parchment,
through this, the Holy One, blessed be He, wears Tefillin,
which are
(the Tefillin)
His glory and praise
(as above),
"declared" [being] a term of importance and praise.
And the reason for this—that it is within the power of Israel that through their fulfillment of the commandments there will be the fulfillment of the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He—
the verse continues,
"And G-d has declared you... to be for Him a treasured people."
And this is what concludes
(in the verse "And G-d has declared you")
"and to keep all His commandments"
(even though, seemingly, this belongs in the verse "You have declared G-d,"
for the praise with which Israel praises the Holy One, blessed be He, is that they accepted upon themselves to be for You a G-d, etc., and to keep His statutes and commandments, etc.),
for "to keep all His commandments" of Israel brings about His commandments,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, will perform the commandments.
Therefore, this is stated in the verse "And G-d has declared you"
(in the praise with which the Holy One, blessed be He, praises Israel),
because this—that it is within the power of Israel to bring about
(through their fulfillment of the commandments)
the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He—
is a great praise for Israel.
And it may be said
that this is what the Rashba said, that the matter of "declared" and "has declared you" is in the manner of "My Beloved is mine and I am His"
(first "My Beloved is mine" and then "and I am His"),
for the power in Israel to be "You have declared G-d,"
to add
(as it were)
importance and praise to the Holy One, blessed be He,
is through this—that "G-d has declared you."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Israel being a treasured people is not due to their merits but solely from G-d's free choice, rooted in their essence, and that G-d's true praise is Israel themselves, not the additional light they generate.
section.t: And "D)"
Now, this—that "G-d has declared you to be for Him a treasured people"—
is not from the aspect of reason,
from the aspect of the virtue of Israel,
their fulfillment of Torah and commandments and the like,
but rather,
that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose [them] in His choice
(free),
as it is written,
"For Yaakov has G-d chosen for Himself, Israel as His treasured possession."
For this—that Israel are His treasured possession—is from the aspect of His choice,
and therefore,
this is in the very essence of Israel.
For each and every one of Israel
(even before he fulfills Torah and commandments)
is His treasured possession.
And through this, there is also brought about in them a virtue
(in the matter of revelations),
that through their fulfillment of the commandments, His commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He, are brought about.
And this is what is written in the Tefillin of the Master of the World
(not the verse "Hear O Israel... G-d is One,"
but rather)
"And who is like Your people Israel, etc.,"
for the primary glory and praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, is not the additional light that is made above
(the fulfillment of the commandments of the Holy One, blessed be He)
which is made through the fulfillment of the commandments of Israel,
but rather,
the praise of Israel themselves,
for this specifically reaches into
(the choice of)
the Essence.
